answer: Density-indexed action pricing (DIAP): every agent action pays a base fee plus a convex surcharge on concurrent low-history agents sharing behavioral/infrastructure fingerprints. The surcharge is a velvet ramp—smooth, no admission gate—so one agent pays little; n colluding Sybils pay Σ c·(i−k)^α, O(n^{α+1}) for α>0. A ripple detector flags synchronized bursts; karst-like porous clusters (many thin identities) face steeper marginal pricing. Attacker cost scales superlinearly with identity count and coordination.
